markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Existing margins measure discrimination against supplied negatives, not useful purchases or compatibility. (2) Feedback suggests broad associations sometimes outweigh current interests; intent and fulfilled needs remain unobserved. (3) Existing scoring hooks support frozen-HSTU probes without another predictor. Training-loader probes cannot establish validation performance.

**Related work.** (1) *Does It Look Sequential?* motivates history perturbations; HSTU’s relative biases make deletion sensitive to position, time, and readout changes. (2) TREC separates unknown compatibility from demonstrated incompatibility; judgments need source-backed title/description evidence. (3) Prakash and Ekstrand motivate popularity strata and heterogeneous outcomes. PyTorch documentation motivates isolated diagnostic data, RNG preservation, and exact mode restoration.

### Framework and directions

| Direction | Observable evidence | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal dependence | Paired score/rank changes | Content versus structural sensitivity |
| Relationship evidence | Source-backed attributes | Sparse or ambiguous compatibility |
| Ranking heterogeneity | Training-frequency/history-length strata | Benefits hidden by averages |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and negative assessment.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paired recent-versus-older deletion [HSTU; sequentiality study] | **4:** controlled adaptation; established ablations | **7:** actionable hypothesis; structurally confounded | **4:** existing hooks; isolation needs care |
| Evidence-backed compatibility audit [TREC] | **5:** explicit conflicts; familiar extraction | **7:** interpretable; limited coverage | **6:** rules feasible; normalization needs auditing |
| Popularity-stratified margins [Prakash; Ekstrand] | **3:** exposes disparities; standard method | **6:** guides sampling; sampled margins may mislead | **2:** counts suffice; small strata noisy |
| Matched identity replacement [HSTU implementation] | **4:** controlled comparator; familiar perturbation | **7:** preserves anchor/positions; replacements imperfect | **5:** batchable; timestamp handling needs verification |

### Selected idea: paired temporal-dependence probe

At 0% progress, retain deletion as a cheap behavioral diagnostic, adding matched identity replacement as a control. Remove the latest event versus one seeded older event; preserve chronology, left padding, and identical targets. Report score and margin contrasts, counts, and anchor changes. Deletion measures total intervention sensitivity: latest deletion changes readout; interior deletion changes relative distances; query timestamps may also change.

```text
cache fixed diagnostic examples independently of training iteration
snapshot RNG states and every submodule mode
try: evaluate paired original/deleted/replaced histories in inference mode
     read final nonpadding position; score identical targets
     record older-minus-recent score and margin contrasts
finally: restore RNG states and every submodule mode
```

Replace recent/older identities at unchanged positions using several training-frequency-matched items; retain timestamps where supported. Neither control establishes causal intent. Preserved-position attention exclusion additionally requires explicit mask/bias support and remains optional.

Preserve required interfaces, existing metrics, explicit definitions, and unavailable statuses. The loader lacks user IDs: report row-level summaries without user-bootstrap claims. For future authorized candidate diagnostics, use fixed rankings, deterministic ties, and user-paired uncertainty; logits are unsuitable for uncalibrated cross-model comparisons.

Freeze probe examples and rules before inspecting effects; never optimize diagnostic sensitivity itself. Any intervention must improve unchanged macro validation HR@10. Keep seed 42, four routed HSTU models, one checkpoint each, and consistent predictor semantics.

idea.description: Strengthen the paired recent-versus-older event removal diagnostic with explicit accounting for HSTU structural confounds, isolated diagnostic execution, and a matched item-identity replacement control. Measure fixed-target score and sampled positive–negative margin contrasts within each frozen category model.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests insufficient alignment with specific current interests, while existing probes measure embedding alignment and sampled ranking separation. Paired deletion can reveal differential dependence on recent and older events, but deletion also changes positional relationships, potentially temporal biases, and sometimes the readout anchor. Identity replacement provides a complementary sensitivity check with fewer structural changes. Neither measurement establishes user intent, compatibility, satisfied needs, or improved recommendation quality.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), all existing metric keys, and the host ModelView interfaces. Use view.model as the actual trained module, view.log2feats and view.predict_score for scoring, and view.item_emb for the existing embedding probe. Do not change training architecture or predictor semantics for the basic diagnostic; keep exactly one independently trained HSTU checkpoint per category.

Do not consume the live training iterator. Supply a separate diagnostic loader with its own seed-42 torch.Generator and explicit worker initialization, or fixed examples cached during preprocessing without advancing the training sampler. Use at most ten diagnostic batches, retaining their order, batch size, example identifiers when available, and a reproducible fingerprint. A local diagnostic generator must not change the seed-42 training stream. Preserve Python and NumPy RNG states and all explicit generator states; use torch.random.fork_rng for CPU and the active CUDA device. Snapshot every submodule's training flag, call model.eval(), execute under torch.inference_mode(), and restore every saved flag and RNG state in finally, including after exceptions. Restore individual flags rather than calling model.train(saved_root_flag), which can overwrite mixed submodule modes. This isolation does not restore an already-consumed loader's worker queues or sampler progress.

For each row, select the final position t with valid nonpadding positive and negative targets. Use only nonpadding events in sequence[row, :t+1], preventing future-context leakage, and require at least two events. Rows with invalid targets or insufficient history must increment explicit skipped counters. Select one older event uniformly from all events except the latest using a local seed-42 generator. Compare the original history, latest-event deletion, and older-event deletion. Compact retained events chronologically and left-pad to the original width. Preserve event-associated timestamps where exposed; inspect the actual supplied backbone before assuming how query times are constructed. The required B x L loader alone does not expose timestamps, so mark temporal-bias controls unavailable unless aligned timestamps are accessible through a verified interface. Always read the final nonpadding position by masked position indices, never count-1.

Use identical positive and negative candidate IDs across conditions. Define D_recent = s_original - s_recent_removed and D_older = s_original - s_older_removed. Their paired contrast D_recent - D_older equals s_older_removed - s_recent_removed; apply the same definition to positive–negative margins. Report means, medians, tenth percentiles, positive-contrast fractions, eligible/skipped counts, and the exact perturbation definitions. Positive contrasts indicate greater sensitivity to latest-event deletion under these operations. They do not isolate content importance: latest deletion changes the readout event; interior deletion changes relative distances across the removed position; absolute embeddings, if present, may shift; and HSTU query-time construction may change temporal biases. Retain the original embedding sample cap of 2,048 real items and existing margin definitions. Empty measurements must be null/unavailable with counts rather than healthy-looking zeros. Category breakdowns remain empty because category metadata is unavailable.

Add identity replacement as a separately labeled control when feasible. For each selected recent/older event, replace only its item ID at the same occupied position, preserving sequence width, masks, position IDs, and timestamps wherever those inputs are supported. Define ten training-frequency bins by sorting real item IDs by (training interaction count, item ID) and splitting into equally sized bins. Draw up to three distinct replacements uniformly from the selected item's bin, excluding padding, reserved tokens, observed prefix items, the positive target, and the supplied negative. Use only training counts, a separate seed-42 generator, and report replacement eligibility and counts. Average replacement effects within an example before aggregating. Replacements are frequency matched perturbations, not observed irrelevant events or confirmed negatives, and can introduce unfamiliar combinations. Latest identity replacement retains the readout position but changes its content; it therefore remains a total network-response measurement rather than a pure attention attribution. Excluding a historical event while preserving original position IDs and the retained-pair bias submatrix is an optional additional control requiring verified attention-mask and relative-bias support; do not approximate it by replacing an interior event with padding. Bias-disabled, position-only, time-only, or residual-bypass probes introduce distribution shift and are not required for this first implementation.

The supplied loader yields None instead of user IDs. Report descriptive row-level statistics and do not claim user-level bootstrap confidence intervals; multiple rows may belong to the same user. If a separate authorized diagnostic dataset provides stable user IDs, first aggregate paired effects per user, then per category, and macro-average the four category means. Bootstrap users within category for uncertainty, explicitly conditional on the frozen model, candidates, and perturbations. A missing category makes the four-category macro diagnostic unavailable rather than silently changing its denominator.

For later authorized candidate-ranking diagnostics, freeze users, candidates, perturbations, and tie handling. Rank by descending score with ascending item ID as the tie breaker; report target-rank changes, HR@10 changes, top-10 overlap divided by 10, and Spearman correlation across scores aligned to the same candidate IDs using average ranks for ties. Report constant-score correlations as undefined with counts. The current one-positive/one-negative loader cannot support these candidate-ranking metrics. Logit contrasts are useful within a frozen model but not calibrated cross-model effect sizes. Supplementary ranking diagnostics must not replace or alter the pinned host evaluator.

Retain diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) and include measured values, definitions, counts, unavailable reasons, structural confounds, and data limitations. No review ratings/text, item categories/prices/stores, simulator traits, ownership, or satisfied needs may be inferred as observed facts. Fix probe rules and cached examples before examining outcomes; do not select checkpoints for high recency sensitivity. Any subsequent training intervention must be selected by unchanged macro validation HR@10, with preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Preserve all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and the shared search budget. No experiments or measured improvements are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
examples = fixed_diagnostic_examples_from_independent_loader(max_batches=10)
saved_modes = [(module, module.training) for module in view.model.modules()]
saved_rng = snapshot_python_numpy_and_explicit_generators()
try:
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[active_cuda_device] if using_cuda else []):
        view.model.eval()
        with torch.inference_mode():
            for row in examples:
                t = final_position_with_valid_positive_and_negative(row)
                history = ordered_nonpadding_prefix(row.sequence, end=t)
                if t is unavailable or len(history) < 2:
                    increment_skipped_reason(); continue
                p, n = row.positive[t], row.negative[t]
                j = local_deletion_rng.choice(range(len(history) - 1))
                conditions = {
                    'original': left_pad(history),
                    'recent_removed': left_pad(history[:-1]),
                    'older_removed': left_pad(remove_event(history, j))
                }
                # Carry aligned timestamps only if the actual model interface exposes them.
                for name, sequence in conditions.items():
                    features = view.log2feats(sequence)
                    h = features[final_nonpadding_position(sequence)]
                    score[name] = view.predict_score(h, p)
                    margin[name] = score[name] - view.predict_score(h, n)
                record(score['older_removed'] - score['recent_removed'])
                record(margin['older_removed'] - margin['recent_removed'])
                for event_index in [len(history) - 1, j]:
                    replacements = sample_up_to_three_frequency_bin_items(
                        history[event_index], exclude=history + [p, n],
                        rng=local_replacement_rng)
                    evaluate_identity_replacements_at_unchanged_positions(
                        history, event_index, replacements, candidates=[p, n])
                    average_replacement_effects_within_example()
finally:
    restore_python_numpy_and_explicit_generators(saved_rng)
    for module, saved_flag in saved_modes:
        module.training = saved_flag
summarize_rows_with_counts_and_unavailable_statuses()
# Aggregate by user only when stable user identifiers actually exist.
return {'metrics': existing_and_new_measured_metrics,
        'metric_definitions': definitions_confounds_and_limitations}

originality.positive: Combines paired temporal perturbations, HSTU-specific structural accounting, and a reproducible diagnostic contract around a concrete feedback-derived hypothesis.
originality.negative: Deletion, matched replacement, and ranking-stability diagnostics are established methods; the contribution is a careful application rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish hypotheses worth testing before spending the limited training budget and provides reusable controls for later HSTU interventions.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may not predict validation gains, and available histories cannot identify intent, compatibility, or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: The basic deletion and replacement probes use existing scoring hooks without retraining or changing prediction.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent data loading, exact RNG/mode restoration, timestamp verification, replacement sampling, and missing-data accounting add work; preserved-bias masking would be a separate, harder extension.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces the HSTU sequential-transduction backbone that must remain the model family.
Motivates accounting for content-dependent aggregation and relative positional/temporal biases when interpreting perturbations.
limitations: Does not establish that history sensitivity measures recent intent or product compatibility.
Architectural descriptions do not establish the behavior of the supplied corrected implementation without verification.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Motivates evaluating sequential dependence through controlled history perturbations.
limitations: Perturbation effects describe model behavior, vary across datasets, and do not establish causal user preferences.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Product Recommendation Guidelines
contributions: Distinguishes substitutes, complements, unknown compatibility, and incompatible complements.
limitations: Applying these distinctions requires evidence that may be missing from available titles and descriptions.
Observed purchases alone do not establish ownership, fulfilled needs, or unwanted substitutes.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): Sequential Recommendation and Negative Sampling
contributions: Motivates examining popularity-dependent trade-offs when interpreting negative-sampling results.
limitations: Reported trade-offs do not establish that a particular unobserved item is a false negative.
Frequency-matched replacement does not establish semantic irrelevance.

related_work.title: Ekstrand et al. (2024): Distributional Evaluation
contributions: Supports examining heterogeneous outcomes and uncertainty beyond aggregate ranking metrics.
limitations: User-level uncertainty estimates require identifiable user observations.
Bootstrap intervals from a frozen model do not capture training variability.

related_work.title: PyTorch Random Number Generator Documentation
contributions: Documents RNG state management and fork_rng for isolated CPU/CUDA random operations.
limitations: Torch RNG restoration alone does not restore Python/NumPy randomness, explicit generators, or DataLoader progress.

related_work.title: PyTorch DataLoader Documentation
contributions: Documents loader generators, worker initialization, sampling, and multiprocessing behavior relevant to independent diagnostic loading.
limitations: Resetting global RNG states does not rewind consumed sampler positions, worker RNG states, or prefetch queues.

related_work.title: PyTorch Module Documentation
contributions: Documents evaluation/training mode semantics underlying per-submodule mode preservation.
limitations: Evaluation mode does not disable autograd.
Recursively restoring the root training mode can overwrite deliberately mixed submodule modes.

related_work.title: PyTorch Autograd Guidance
contributions: Distinguishes evaluation mode from gradient modes and explains inference-mode execution.
limitations: Inference mode does not independently disable dropout or preserve RNG and module state.

related_work.title: Meta Generative Recommenders: HSTU Reference Implementation
contributions: Provides implementation context for HSTU aggregation and relative position/time bias handling.
Motivates checking shifted query timestamps and attention masks before interpreting deletion effects.
limitations: The supplied corrected backbone may differ from this reference.
Deletion-confound statements are architectural deductions, not published causal attribution results.

related_work.title: HSTU Relative Position and Temporal Bias Ablations
contributions: Provides evidence that positional and temporal bias choices can affect recommendation quality.
limitations: These ablations do not isolate content importance in recent-versus-older deletion probes.
Disabling biases at inference can introduce distribution shift.

related_work.title: SciPy Spearman Rank Correlation Documentation
contributions: Defines rank correlation and handling relevant to supplementary candidate-ranking stability diagnostics.
limitations: Constant inputs produce undefined correlation.
Rank agreement does not establish recommendation quality, and the supplied two-candidate training probe cannot measure HR@10.
